summary: The Chiang Mai Marathon 10 km is confirmed for Sunday 20 December 2026, starting and finishing at Tha Phae Gate. It offers the atmosphere of the flagship race with straightforward city logistics. The 90-minute cutoff still requires purposeful running or a brisk run/walk, so choose it according to your training rather than treating it as casual sightseeing.
whyGo: Join the city’s international race without committing to a half or full marathon.
Return to the same landmark gate after a course the organiser describes as flat.
bestFor: Recreational runners already comfortable covering 10 km.
Travellers staying near the Old City who want a memorable early-morning activity.
skipIf: You cannot comfortably cover 10 km inside 90 minutes, equivalent to 9 minutes per kilometre.
Your arrival leaves no time to collect your race pack or sleep before the early start.
duration: Allow roughly 2–3 hours including staging and recovery; this is a planning estimate. Race window: 05:00–06:30.
cost: Published overseas/foreigner entry: THB700 through 31 October, THB800 on 1–20 November, or THB1,000 on 1–15 December, plus processing charges. Thai-national fees differ.
hours: Race: 20 December, 05:00 start and 06:30 cutoff. 10 km/3 km bag service: 03:30–04:50. Awards: 07:00–08:30.
bestTime: Plan to reach the start area around 04:15–04:30; this is a suggested buffer, subject to final runner instructions.
gettingThere: Tha Phae Gate is on the eastern edge of the Old City. Nearby accommodation makes walking practical. If staying farther away, arrange an overnight taxi beforehand and allow for race traffic; exact road closures remain unconfirmed.
booking: Enter through the registration link on the official website and check confirmation using passport details. Fees are non-refundable. Collect your pack at Tha Phae Gate on 18–19 December, 10:00–18:00; bring passport identification or a phone photograph.
accessibility: Published 10 km age groups begin at 16. Wheelchair entry, accessible toilets and assistance arrangements are not specified; confirm individual requirements with the organiser.
practicalTips: Keep the preceding evening quiet and lay out your bib, shoes and transport plan before bed.
Check final course, aid-station and baggage instructions rather than relying on older route maps.
Leave time for breakfast and rest before booking another demanding outing.
decemberNotes: These dates explicitly refer to December 2026. Expect darkness at the start and check the weather forecast close to race day. Runners landing after 17:00 on 19 December are directed to email the organiser about exceptional pack collection.
uncertainties: Remaining entry availability, final road closures, aid-station details and accessible facilities were not established.
The photograph shows a historical race, not the forthcoming 2026 10 km.
